Test-retest stability of a judge

Source: R/stability.R
test_retest.Rd

Re-grades the same items and reports chance-corrected agreement plus mean pairwise disagreement. any_flip_rate_at_n_runs is retained as a descriptive quantity but must not be compared across different n_runs, because it rises mechanically as more opportunities to flip are observed.

Usage

test_retest(
  data,
  judge,
  input_cols = NULL,
  id_col = NULL,
  n_runs = 5,
  seed = NULL,
  label_levels = NULL,
  weights = c("unweighted", "linear", "quadratic", "ordinal"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  n_boot = 1000,
  audit_id = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of items to grade.

judge

A judge function (data) -> labels.

input_cols

Columns visible to judge. Required so labels and other audit-only fields are not passed through accidentally.

id_col

Optional unique source identifier. It is validated but is not exposed to the judge unless explicitly included in input_cols.

n_runs

Number of repeated gradings; must be at least two.

seed

Optional R random seed. This does not force deterministic behavior from a remote model provider.

label_levels

Optional complete label universe. Unweighted, a declared level no run used changes no coefficient. Weighted, the weights come from the full declared scale, so an unused level can still change AC2; see agreement().

weights

Agreement weights passed to Gwet's coefficient; see agreement() for the weight schemes.

conf_level

Confidence level for every interval.

n_boot

Number of item-bootstrap resamples.

audit_id

Optional evidence-bundle identifier. Use the same value as the related calibration and bias probes.

Value

A yourhonor_stability object with raw runs, per-item evidence, missingness, pairwise disagreement, Gwet agreement, and intervals. stability_status explains why chance-corrected agreement is unavailable; in particular, one observed category is insufficient_variation, not perfect AC1/AC2, and stability_conf_low and stability_conf_high are then NA. The pairwise-disagreement interval remains available.

The pairwise-disagreement interval is a hybrid: the percentile item bootstrap widened to include a Wilson score interval for the mean per-item disagreement over n_items_scored items. The Wilson interval keeps a zero-disagreement sample from producing a zero-width interval and typically sets both bounds once n_runs > 2, so this interval is conservative relative to the bootstrap alone and widens only, never narrows. The chance-corrected interval is the plain item bootstrap.

Missing judgments are left out of the observed statistics, so a judge that abstains where it would have been unstable looks stable there. The worst-case fields bound that: pairwise_disagreement_worst_case is the mean over all n_items items of a per-item disagreement in which every pair involving a missing judgment disagrees (an item with fewer than two judgments counts as 1; per_item$pairwise_disagreement_worst_case holds the per-item values), and pairwise_disagreement_worst_case_high is its upper bound, computed like the observed one on the same bootstrap draws and never below pairwise_disagreement_conf_high. With no missing judgment it equals pairwise_disagreement_conf_high, and it is NA when that is (no item has two judgments). This is the upper bound acceptance_policy() assesses. A numeric NaN judgment is missing, not a label.

any_flip_rate_at_n_runs is over the n_items_complete items with every run observed (NA when there are none), since an incomplete item had fewer chances to flip; under selective abstention it describes complete items only. any_flip_rate_worst_case counts every item with an observed flip or a missing judgment as flipped, over all n_items.

runs holds labels in source-row order. Because every run is graded under a fresh shuffled key, judge_item_ids is an integer matrix parallel to runs whose entry [i, r] is the .item_id the judge saw for source row i in run r; join judge-side logs on that key, never on the row number.

Examples

noisy_judge <- function(d) sample(c("C", "P"), nrow(d), replace = TRUE)
data <- tibble::tibble(input = paste("answer", 1:10))
test_retest(data, noisy_judge, input_cols = "input",
            n_runs = 4, n_boot = 100, seed = 1)
#> 
#> ── yourhonor test-retest stability ──
#> 
#> 4 runs - pairwise disagreement 0.45 [0.20, 0.73].
#> gwet_ac1: 0.12 [-0.15, 0.52].
#> Any-flip rate at exactly 4 runs: 0.80; missing judgments: 0.00.
